purpose: Test the first graph-structural/holographic contraction proposed after v8.5.5: can the exact six-leg GF(3) current signature be put directly into a symmetric domain-3 Holant class by one uniform invertible basis, or into a nontrivial tensor product class by arbitrary invertible portwise basis changes? Both routes admit exact basis-invariant local obstructions.

local_signature.definition: F(k)=0 unless sum_i k_i=0 in GF(3); on the conservation hyperplane F(k)=h(k.v_plus)+h(k.v_minus).
local_signature.support: Exactly the 243-point five-dimensional conservation hyperplane sum_i k_i=0; F never vanishes on that hyperplane.

uniform_holographic_symmetry_obstruction.basis_invariance_lemma: For any invertible 3x3 matrix T over any characteristic-zero field, the permutation action P_sigma on tensor legs commutes with T^{tensor 6}. Hence P_sigma(T^{tensor 6}F)=T^{tensor 6}F iff P_sigma F=F. Therefore the full leg-permutation stabilizer is unchanged by every uniform invertible holographic basis transformation.
uniform_holographic_symmetry_obstruction.consequence: Because the stabilizer has order 4 rather than 6!=720, no uniform invertible basis can turn F into a fully symmetric six-ary signature. In particular the 2025 Cai-Ihm Holant*_3 dichotomy for symmetric real-valued signatures cannot be imported to this local tensor merely by a standard uniform orthogonal/invertible basis change.
uniform_holographic_symmetry_obstruction.scope: This does not exclude port-dependent gauges, bipartite two-sided transforms, gadget reductions, or tractable asymmetric Holant classes.

portwise_product_obstruction.flattening_rank_field: Q (hence also R/C rank for this integer tensor)

rank_profiles.2|4: rank 3 on 1 cut, rank 6 on 6 cuts, rank 9 on 8 cuts
rank_profiles.3|3: rank 6 on 4 cuts, rank 9 on 8 cuts, rank 12 on 8 cuts

portwise_product_obstruction.basis_invariance_lemma: Under arbitrary invertible portwise changes T_1 tensor ... tensor T_6, every bipartition flattening is multiplied on the left and right by invertible Kronecker matrices, so its rank is invariant.
portwise_product_obstruction.consequence: Every nontrivial bipartition has rank greater than one. Therefore no invertible portwise basis can make F factor as a tensor product across any nontrivial split of the six ports. This closes the direct product-separable contraction route.
portwise_product_obstruction.scope: This does not rule out sums of product tensors, matchgate/Pfaffian structures, bounded-rank tensor networks using auxiliary indices, or graph-global cancellations.
